raw_segments.text: Duke, why should I not, had I the heart to do it, like to the Egyptian thief at point
of death, kill what I love?
A savage jealousy that sometimes savors nobly.
But hear me this, since you to nonregardance cast my faith, and that I partly know the
instrument that screws me from my true place in your favor, live you the marble-breasted
But this your minion, whom I know you love, and whom, by heaven I swear, I tender dearly,
him will I tear out of that cruel eye where he sits crowned in his master's spite.
Come boy with me, my thoughts are ripe in mischief, I'll sacrifice the lamb that I
do love, to spite a raven's heart within a dove.
